text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian consumers, already battling price increases brought about by petrol shortages, now face higher prices for kerosene and cooking gas, as a result of scarcity.
- The ruling military council may reschedule all elections, which have to be held under the transition to democracy programme, to June 1998.
- A court has ordered Royal Dutch Shell's Nigerian unit, to pay 30 million naira as compensation to local communities in mid-western Nigeria for an oil spillage in 1982.
- The Petroleum Trust Fund has given 700 million naira to the Nigerian Railways Corporation for renovation of 250 railway stations.
- A World Bank report has confirmed that Nigeria mismanaged a $12 billion windfall it reaped from higher prices for crude oil during the Gulf War.
